body:
Read together, the criticism and the rival converge on the same correction from different directions, and that convergence is the strongest result available. Neither engages the other; each derives 'diagnose privately before designing publicly' on its own grounds — the criticism from branch analysis (on the out-voted and rigged-process branches, a design meeting the avoider skips manufactures fresh evidence for the grievance), the rival from the standing-defeat reading (attendance as predictable loss). I adopt it, and the grounds are stronger than a preference: reversing the order is nearly free because a private conversation obliges nobody, while a meeting commits all three — an asymmetric bet worth taking at moderate confidence. The companion correction (ob2) follows: p1 is not answerable at the meeting and stops being carried as a meeting question.

The private round uses the rival's questions rather than the account's: 'what does a fair week look like' and 'do the talks feel fair, do you have a real say' are better built against the criticism's meta-risk — asking someone why they avoid chore-talks is still a chore-talk at one remove, while asking what fairness looks like is not. Two precautions are taken from the edges of both pieces: run the same questions with both friends and tell each that you are (the rival's own r14 worry about coalition-appearance dissolves only if the symmetry is visible), and plan for silence in advance (ob5) — silence routes to the floor below, not to a repeat attempt. One self-directed addition: the ledger mechanism applies to the asker too. Walk in assuming your own tally is inflated; it turns the round from audit into listening.

The design goal is revised, not just the order. The rival's ledger claim rests on a real, commonly cited result — partners' estimates of their own shares of household work sum to well past 100 percent — whose exact size is unverifiable here, but nothing below needs the number; the mechanism (each person remembers their own labour vividly) is plausible on its face and predicts the asker's perceptions as much as the friends'. Under-specification (c1) and ledger divergence (r1) are co-possible, and the exposed material cannot choose between them — but they respond differently to written clarity, so the trial with written terms plus a bounded dispute protocol is the discriminator. And because ledger divergence survives clarity, disputes will not reach zero: the goal becomes disagreements that are cheap to finish. That single revision also dissolves the tension the criticism found between checkable specificity (a2) and minimal revisability (o1): if every wording dispute gets exactly one airing at the weekly slot, then settlement by alternation and a bar on reopening, the record's completeness stops being load-bearing and it can afford to be minimal. Two criticisms meeting at one mechanism; take both.

On allocation: ob3 is adopted and the account's either/or rejected as presented — uncapped triggers load the early-home person systematically and mint a new contestable fact in a household that litigates facts. Triggers survive only capped or rotated, and only if the flat actively wants fewer decisions. In place of the plain re-deal I take the rival's rotating proposer/veto: same weekly cadence against actual rosters, but rotation puts the pen in the avoider's hand early, the whole-draft-only veto keeps the meeting at yes/no, and a published default makes a veto cheap. This also answers r4, the one claim here that neither earlier piece contained: convening is a fourth chore, and if the asker becomes permanent house manager the role itself becomes the thing avoided. Rotating authorship is the countermeasure — and since the task is asker-posed, the risk is live by construction.

Standards: r7 converts the account's open p2 into a rule — the house standard is the highest standard all three actually accept, and anything above it belongs to whoever wants it, their labour or their money. It subsumes a5's standards negotiation for the common case; a5's cross-domain trades remain for the case where no common floor exists. The gate matters: 'all three accept' presupposes the avoider's answer from the private round — one more reason design waits. Priced exit: adopted as an option, not a fixture, on the rival's own demotion (chores read as care, not allocation) plus an unknown the material does not settle, comparable budgets. Get the quote, leave it visible, decide items and splits only with prior agreement.

Floor: ob6 is adopted and promoted from fallback to fixture — own dishes and kit, personal zones, permanent single-owner domains (convergent with the rival's r12). Every other remedy presupposes the participation whose absence is itself a symptom; this one is partly unilateral and removes agreements instead of administering them. It runs in parallel from the start, not after failure.

Assembled order: (1) the private round as above; (2) one short meeting framed as fixing the system, mechanisms offered as a menu with the avoider choosing first — the choosing is part of the re-engagement, not a courtesy; (3) a four-week trial with explicit expiry, the dispute protocol running, the record minimal; (4) the floor operating throughout; (5) the rival's r15 branch held in reserve: if the avoider will not engage even with a mechanism they chose, or the round shows the disengagement predates the chores, the question stops being chores, and that conversation is cheaper now than later.

Left open deliberately: whether the asker already knows what the avoider is avoiding (the criticism's pr1 — if so, step 1 is confirmation, not discovery); who should deliver the private round if a two-against-one perception is live; whether alternation should be tallied per person or per pair among three (default per person, untested here); and the actual standards gap, which only the round reveals. If both diagnoses fail in trial, the residue points between particular people, and the friend who left the talks is the only reliable informant — which is where this plan starts.
